text:
Rohan Patel: heads up — since ~08:12 UTC eu-west GPU pools started showing sustained admission > capacity, frontend started 502s and queued requests spiked. Noticing a lot of cross-region reroutes back to hosted which made things worse.
Alex Chen: seeing it too, graphs show controller heartbeats to region nodes dropped around 08:11:45. control-plane reported 3 lost connections then partial recovery. :warning:
Sophie Martinez: logs from adm-controller: 
```
ERROR admission: pool "eu-west-gpu-a" over-allocated: active=132 queued=58 capacity=96
WARN routing: fallback to hosted due to capacity signal missing for region eu-west
```
Maria Gomez: network team — any packet loss or BGP flaps around that time?
Kai Wu: we had an internal mgmt-plane maintenance window at 08:10 for routing fabric upgrades; supposed to be nondisruptive but I see spike in control-plane RTT to eu-west. Might be the cause.
Rohan Patel: hypothesis: mgmt-plane upgrade caused transient control plane split. Regional admission controllers lost health checks so global admission fell back to optimistic admission, over-admitting local pools. That saturated GPUs, triggered eviction and then cross-region reroutes to hosted API, overwhelming hosted pools.
Alex Chen: that matches telemetry — initial queueing was local but within 2m hosted request rate doubled. Hosted autoscale reacted but had cold-start latency leading to client 502s and client retries created additional tail-load.
eng-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2028-1831234567 — "eu-west admission spike -> hosted fallthrough" (severity: P2)
Sophie Martinez: mitigation we did: 08:15 reverted mgmt-plane changes, 08:17 paused cross-region fallback routing, 08:18 applied strict admission cap on eu-west pools (max-admit=capacity) and started draining queued requests to backlog queue. 08:22 restored normal routing.
Maria Gomez: cost note: hosted egress and burst GPU hours increased ~3x for that 15 minute window. Preliminary estimate: ~$12k extra for the incident window.
Kai Wu: action items I'd propose: 1) make mgmt-plane upgrades gate health-checks so admission controllers don't default to optimistic admit; 2) add circuit-breaker on cross-region fallbacks to avoid immediate fanout; 3) automated knob to pause routing fallthroughs during control-plane instability.
Alex Chen: also add a small hysteresis window (30-60s) before scaling hosted to avoid thrash from retries; and add token-based client retry backoff guidance for SDKs.
Rohan Patel: agreed. For RCA writeup: root cause = management-plane upgrade induced transient control-plane split -> admission controllers lacked authoritative capacity -> optimistic admission + fallback routing -> cascade into hosted saturation. Contributing factors = aggressive fallback policy, lack of circuit-breaker, no hysteresis on hosted autoscale.
Sophie Martinez: I'll draft the incident blameless postmortem and include graphs + before/after configs. Will ping infra-diffs for the mgmt-plane gating change.
Maria Gomez: ping finance for cost chargeback.
Kai Wu: I'll open the routing-policy MR with circuit-breaker and add tests simulating control-plane partition.
Alex Chen: can we also add a canary for mgmt-plane upgrades that simulates control-plane disconnects in staging?
Rohan Patel: yes. Next steps: Sophie will own postmortem (eta tomorrow EOD), Kai will own routing MR (eta 1 week), Alex will adjust autoscale hysteresis (eta 3 days), Maria will track cost and billing.
Sophie Martinez: thanks — adding notes to the incident doc and will drop link when ready. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Deploy rollback executed at 08:15 by Kai Wu (reason: mgmt-plane instability).
Rohan Patel: wrapping up — no customer-facing outage page yet, but we should coordinate a short incident summary for SRE and support channels.
Maria Gomez: noted, I'll draft a short incident summary for support.
Alex Chen: great, keep updates here. :eyes:
